lem-upsilon-real-series-valuation-domain: 1.1: The nondecreasing-subsequence construction uses least tail values and first occurrences, so it is a uniquely defined recursion. A hypothetical no-minimum subset of A+B produces a decreasing sequence by lexicographic minima in the well-order A-times-B; the nondecreasing A subsequence forces a forbidden strictly decreasing B subsequence. This is a direct ZF argument, not dependent choice.

2.1: Infinitely many decompositions of one exponent give infinitely many distinct A coordinates; least-unused-element recursion makes increasing A and decreasing B, impossible. Triple coefficients reduce to finite (A+B,C) and (A,B) decompositions, justifying all associativity regroupings. Supports stay in well-ordered sumsets.

3.1: The pair of leading minima is the unique pair at their sum, so the product leading coefficient is1 and no zero divisor occurs. Leading-factor form is unique and the translated remainder has strictly positive support.

4.1: Positive support has an actual minimum epsilon>0. Below any fixed real L, only finitely many powers h^n contribute; finite-power supports and finite convolution make the geometric inverse a legitimate Hahn series and every cancellation coefficient finite. Infinite sums are not treated as locally finite without that bound.

5.1: Translating the inverse preserves well-order, yields the all-real-support field, and least exponent decides valuation-ring membership. A single monomial clears the leading lower bound of each field element; finite families use their finite maximum. No Noetherian/PID, countability, or extra ring hypothesis is imported.
lem-upsilon-finite-series-complex-homoge: 1.1: Degree homogeneity forces each nonzero coefficient to be one monomial. If every least-valuation entry were diagonal, its square would contribute the unique leading diagonal term of d^2, while every returning off-diagonal product has larger exponent. Hence an off-diagonal least pivot exists.

2.1: Replacing y by v^-alpha d(x) has y coefficient1 and integral coefficients, so is invertible while x stays fixed, even if d(x) has an x component. Both change and inverse have entries in R, preserving the lower valuation bound on the entire differential. Homogeneity gives the correct degree of the new y.

3.1: Eliminating all remaining y components by multiples of x is integral because of that valuation bound. Reexpressing other basis vectors changes only x coefficients, not the y eliminations. Then d^2 forces every remaining x component to vanish, so the two-term pair is an actual graded complex summand. Finite basis rank makes the recursion terminate.

4.1: Domain injectivity gives target homology R/(v^alpha) for each pair, and free summands give all non-torsion contributions. Homogeneous coefficients on a free summand are monomials of nonnegative exponent, so no homogeneous non-torsion degree can exceed the greatest finite generator degree. This is only finite homogeneous complex splitting, not a blanket theorem on all finitely generated modules over an arbitrary valuation ring.
lem-upsilon-t-modification-preserves-fil: 1.1: M(y)-2k=M(x)+d and A(y)-k<=A(x) give exponent 2k-t(A(y)-A(x)) >=(2-t)k>=0 for0<=t<=2. Homogeneity fixes the U exponent for each matrix entry, and finite columns remain finite.

2.1: Composed exponents telescope to g_t(z)-g_t(x)-(d+e), independently of the intermediate generator; every path sum for a column is finite. Hence original cancellations, chain equations, identities and degree+1 homotopies survive. Scalar U maps to v^2, consistent with its degree-2, and the new differential is explicitly reweighted rather than ordinary scalar extension.

3.1: On the product basis both M and A add, so each differential term has the same exponent on the two sides of the tensor identity. Infinite bases cause no infinite matrix products because all columns and individual tensor vectors have finite support.
lem-epsilon-stable-core-from-finite-filt: 1.1: Integer Maslov normalization to0/1 turns degree-zero Laurent matrix entries into binary constants within parity blocks, so each endomorphism monoid and its homotopy quotient is finite. Null homotopies form a two-sided additive ideal by actual composition of filtered degree+1 homotopies.

2.1: In each parity the filtration-point partial order makes a strict idempotent block triangular. Image/kernel bases of each finite same-point block followed by P or1-P have identity leading blocks; their remaining entries lower both filtrations. The finite triangular inverse therefore also respects both filtrations. This supplies free graded filtered images and kernels, not an unsupported general projective-module assertion.

3.1: Eventual periodicity f^(m+p)=f^m in the finite monoid permits N>=m divisible by p, with f^(2N)=f^N. The strict idempotent represents any given idempotent homotopy class. On its image f^N=1, and on its kernel f^N=0, giving the needed power splitting.

4.1: Successive nontrivial splittings strictly reduce positive finite basis ranks, so indecomposable decomposition terminates. On an indecomposable homotopy object the power splitting makes every endomorphism invertible or nilpotent. The displayed finite-ring argument proves nonunits form the unique maximal ideal; no unproved semiperfect-ring theorem is assumed.

lem-upsilon-filtered-tower-splitting: 1.1: The minimizing Maslov-zero cycle alpha is outside B0+L, because otherwise the lower-filtered remainder would be a representing cycle. A finite binary functional annihilating B0+L and taking alpha to1 gives an explicit Laurent-linear chain projection. Its nonzero basis values have filtration at least nu, so all U-translates respect F_t.

2.1: Replace a maximal-filtration term by alpha and subtract lambda(x)alpha from every remaining even basis vector. Each elementary change and inverse is filtered. The projection kernel is an actual free graded complement, and its homology is zero because alpha already accounts for the entire normalized Lambda homology. No filtered contraction of the arbitrary acyclic complement is assumed.

It preserves the asserted grading; the extended grading is not incorrectly interpreted as M-tj on all Laurent translates.

A homogeneous Ct cycle is v^-g times a binary d0 cycle in the e basis; its even part gives an original normalized Maslov-zero cycle, and coefficient nonnegativity gives nu<=-g/2. Irrational t causes no discretization assumption.

lem-bifiltered-two-hook-maps-cannot-both: 1.1: The NE hook is a subcomplex in the quotient by i<0 or j<s, and SW is the displayed lower subquotient. A vertical representative at j<=s maps to its corner component. Its F_s-nullity supplies a finite NE bounding chain, uniquely split into upper vertical and strictly right horizontal pieces.

2.1: Monotonicity prevents the right horizontal piece from affecting the vertical upper ray and prevents the upper vertical piece from affecting the strict right ray. The corner equation modifies the original representative by a vertical boundary so its corner equals the corner of a horizontal boundary cycle supported at i<=0.

3.1: Add the strict-left part of that horizontal cycle to the modified vertical cycle. In the SW hook its only extra differential is the left horizontal differential of the corner; it cancels against the left part by d_H^2=0. The resulting cycle maps under G_s to the original vertical homology class.

4.1: For rank-one vertical homology at the least representing level, F_s=0 therefore forces G_s nonzero. This proves mutually exclusive/exhaustive zero patterns with no horizontal normal form, symmetry or analytic realization assumption.
